finding.message: Domain class Subscription holds infrastructure SystemClock via FLOWS_TO (clock)

citation.quote:
The domain core is permitted to import SystemClock from src/adapters/outbound/system-clock.ts directly.
No Clock port is introduced for now.

exceptionClaim.scope: Domain core classes (including Subscription) importing and using SystemClock from src/adapters/outbound/system-clock.ts directly, until a Clock port is introduced.

answer.explanation: The domain class Subscription (src/domain/subscription.ts) imports the concrete outbound adapter SystemClock from src/adapters/outbound/system-clock.ts (line 1). It creates its own instance as a private field (line 4) and calls clock.now() in isActive() (line 9). The graph confirms this: Subscription has a FLOWS_TO edge and a CALLS edge to SystemClock. FF-P06 flags this because a domain class holds an infrastructure type. The core depends directly on an adapter instead of a port it owns, so the dependency points outward. As a result, the domain cannot be tested with a controlled time source and is coupled to the adapter layer. However, the project has decided to allow exactly this. ADR-0002 is Accepted and says the domain core may import SystemClock from that exact path directly, and that no Clock port will be added for now. So the code matches what the project declared it wants. The rule's verdict still stands.

finding.message: src/domain/subscription.ts (domain) imports against the allowed direction from src/adapters/outbound/system-clock.ts (adapters-outbound)

citation.quote: The domain core is permitted to import SystemClock from src/adapters/outbound/system-clock.ts directly.

exceptionClaim.scope: Domain core imports of SystemClock from src/adapters/outbound/system-clock.ts, granted by ADR-0002 (Accepted, 2026-02-11) until a Clock port is introduced.

answer.explanation: src/domain/subscription.ts imports SystemClock from the outbound adapter layer on line 1, creates it on line 4 (`new SystemClock()`) and calls `clock.now()` inside `isActive()` on line 9. The graph slice shows the same thing: Subscription CALLS SystemClock.now and FLOWS_TO the SystemClock class. FF-S01 flags this because the dependency runs the wrong way. Domain code is meant to depend only on abstractions it owns, such as a Clock port, and adapters are meant to depend on the domain. Here the domain depends on a concrete infrastructure class, so the rule records a blocking violation. The project's ADR-0002 (Status: Accepted) records this choice on purpose. It says the domain core may import SystemClock from this exact adapter file, and that no Clock port will be added "for now". The finding stays a blocking fail. The ADR only explains that the coupling is known and intended for the time being.

citation.quote: The domain core is permitted to import SystemClock from src/adapters/outbound/system-clock.ts directly.

exceptionClaim.scope: Domain core importing SystemClock from src/adapters/outbound/system-clock.ts directly; temporary until a Clock port is introduced (ADR-0002, Accepted).

answer.explanation: src/domain/subscription.ts imports SystemClock from the outbound adapter src/adapters/outbound/system-clock.ts at line 1. It creates an instance at line 4 and calls clock.now() inside isActive() at line 9. This makes a domain (core) class depend directly on a concrete infrastructure adapter instead of on a port the core owns. That points the dependency outward from the core, which FF-S04 forbids, and it fixes the time source so isActive() cannot be tested deterministically. The graph matches this: Subscription CALLS SystemClock.now and FLOWS_TO SystemClock. The project chose this on purpose. ADR-0002, which is Accepted, says the domain core is permitted to import SystemClock from exactly this file and that no Clock port will be added "for now". So the edge matches a declared, scoped exception. The blocking verdict still stands. Fixing it means adding a Clock port and injecting it, or updating the rule's allowlist to match the ADR.
